title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - LumenAI
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer is interested in adding capacity (reserved GPUs), enabling eu-west-1 region, and extending contract term to secure pricing. Discussed benchmarking, SLA targets, KMS for keys, VPC peering and private deployment options. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send updated quote, SE to run region-specific perf tests, customer to confirm budget and procurement timeline.
next_steps: Samira to send updated quote with tiered pricing and 12-month term by 2026-11-09
Diego to run dedicated benchmark in eu-west-1 and share results by 2026-11-12
Marcus to confirm budget and procurement ETA by 2026-11-11
Priya to share SOC 2 + compliance pack link by 2026-11-08
action_items: Samira Patel | Send updated quote with reserved G4 capacity and pricing options | 2026-11-09
Diego Marin | Run load and latency benchmarks in eu-west-1 (p95 target) and upload results | 2026-11-12

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-05 15:00 PT - Duration 42 mins
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Marin (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Marcus Reed, Janelle Park, Omar Khan, Tessa Wong (LumenAI)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - good to see you. We're just doing our quarterly renewal / expansion check-in, figure out capacity and region needs. How's everything on your side Marcus?
[00:15] Marcus: Hey Samira, yeah, thanks. Things are good. We're hitting some capacity limits during peak inference windows for our summarization product. P95 latency creeping up, and our EU customers want data to stay in eu-west so, need region.
[00:30] Janelle: Yeah, and we also want to lock pricing for the next year if possible - our finance team wants predictable costs.
[00:42] Samira: Totally. That makes sense. A couple things we can do - reserved capacity (Dedicated) to guarantee throughput, or add burst capacity. Diego, want to speak to perf implications?
[00:55] Diego: Sure. From a runtime side, reserved G4s give you predictable throughput; we can tune batch sizes and KV cache settings. One note - prefix caching and KV cache savings are pretty big for repetitive prompts but depends on your sequence length distribution.
[01:12] Omar: Quick question on KV cache - is that something we manage or is it automatic? I ask because our infra folks worry about memory footprint on instances.
[01:23] Diego: Good question. It's automatic in the serving runtime, but you can configure cache retention windows. Memory impacts scale with active contexts; with reserved nodes we can size to your active sessions. There's some mis-cue in the auto transcribe - K V cache sometimes shows up as cue-vic in notes, ignore that.
[01:40] Marcus: Also, SSO and key management - we have KMS in GCP for keys. How does Redwood integrate?
[01:48] Priya: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; we can set up envelope encryption and audit logs for all request traces. We'll share a compliance pack.
[02:00] Janelle: For region rollouts, we're focusing eu-west-1 first, then ap-southeast, but eu is higher priority. What's the lead time to enable a new region?
[02:12] Samira: For Hosted customers we can enable region in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity. For Dedicated we recommend a reserved pool in that region - that needs capacity planning; typically 4-8 weeks if new hardware is required. We can do a short pilot in the region with burst.
[02:28] Tessa: From procurement - if we extend term to 12 months and commit to X reserved capacity, can we get a discount?
[02:36] Samira: Yes - we can do tiered discounts for committed spend. Diego, margin on longer term?
[02:42] Diego: From an ops perspective, committed capacity helps us optimize placement. We can offer ~10-20% off list for 12 month commit depending on size, plus additional on prepay.
[02:55] Marcus: Okay, good. For the benchmarks - we'd like p95 under 400ms for our 2k token prompts. Can Redwood meet that in eu-west with the model we use (open LLM custom) or will we need a smaller latency model?
[03:10] Diego: We need to run the region-specific perf test. In general G4s with quantization profiles tuned get p95s in the 200-400ms range for your token sizes, but it varies. We'll run the same load and capture p50/p95/p99 and costs.
[03:30] Omar: Network wise we'll want VPC peering and control plane in our VPC. Private deployment maybe?
[03:36] Samira: You have two patterns: Redwood Dedicated with customer VPC peering or Redwood Private if you need fully customer-managed control plane. Dedicated gives isolation plus managed updates; Private is more involved and has a different pricing/ops model.
[03:55] Janelle: Which is easier for SAML/SSO integrations?
[04:00] Priya: Both support SAML/SSO and RBAC; Private gives you direct control of the identity provider flow, but Dedicated supports SSO via the Redwood control plane with SAML assertions and SCIM provisioning.
[04:16] Marcus: Security review - do you have SOC 2 and ISO docs?
[04:20] Priya: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 and ISO certs and the compliance pack after this call.
[04:28] Tessa: Procurement timeline - if we sign 12 months with reserved 8 GPUs in eu-west, we need a quote for budget approval by end of next week.
[04:36] Samira: We'll prioritize that. I'll send an updated quote with a 12-month term and tiered pricing.
[04:44] Diego: I'll schedule the benchmark jobs and share results. Any particular model versions we should test?
[04:50] Marcus: We're on rdx-1.2 (internal shorthand) - I think in Redwood catalog it's the open-llm-v1 variant - there might be naming mismatches in the catalog, watch out.
[05:02] Diego: Okay, we'll verify the exact model id. Sometimes transcription/gdocs calls confuse names - r-d-x versus rdx. We'll confirm the config used in production.
[05:15] Janelle: About cost - can you show token-level cost breakdowns per route? We want to attribute costs to features.
[05:22] Samira: Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. We'll include a sample dashboard screenshot in the quote deck.
[05:32] Omar: One more on SLA - we need 99.9% uptime and latency SLOs. Can you commit?
[05:39] Samira: For Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptimes depending on the contract; the exact SLOs are in the enterprise addendum. We'll surface the SLA terms in the quote. For Hosted we have best-effort with high availability zones but the enterprise SLA is for dedicated customers.
[05:56] Marcus: Great. Also, will there be runbook/operational playbooks for failover?
[06:01] Priya: Yes, we provide runbooks and can collaborate on on-call playbooks for incident response.
[06:08] Tessa: On the procurement side, any compliance add-ons cost? e.g., data residency, extra audit log retention.
[06:14] Priya: Yes, audit log retention beyond the default window and additional compliance services are add-ons. We'll include options in the quote.
[06:25] Samira: To recap - LumenAI wants reserved capacity in eu-west-1, 12-month term, price lock, SOC2 docs, and perf benchmarks for p95<400ms. Redwood will send quote and run benchmarks. Anything else?
[06:38] Marcus: I think that covers it. Also want to check on multi-region routing - can we route EU traffic to eu-west and fall back to us-west on capacity issues?
[06:47] Diego: Yes - smart routing policies can route by geo with automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We can set cost vs latency tradeoffs too.
[07:00] Janelle: Perfect.
[07:02] Samira: Alright team - next steps captured. We'll follow up via email with the quote and benchmark plan. Thanks all.
[07:10] 
[30:00] <note: long benchmarking discussion omitted in transcript export - summary above>

[41:00] Priya: I'll drop the SOC 2 link and architecture diagram into the email thread.
[41:10] Samira: Thanks Priya. Diego, you'll share the perf plan?
[41:16] Diego: Yep, I'll share a script and the results link.
[41:22] Marcus: Appreciate it. That's all from us.
[41:28] Samira: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up.

End of transcript.
